findings.claim: Loop 5 finishes every animation on the checklist and tags whose end time is finite, and treats that as 'the state the learner sees once it has ended'. A finite end time does not mean the animation ever ends on screen. A paused animation, one with an enormous duration, or one with an enormous delay and backwards fill all have finite end times. finish() removes their effect before measuring, while the real page keeps drawing the held keyframe. I added one rule at a time to a private copy of the completed work. Each of these passed all 12 tests although the page as drawn shows the wrong size: a paused animation holding a scale on both tags; a paused animation holding a different width on both tags; a days-long animation holding a scale on both tags; a days-long animation holding a zoom on the gear checklist; and a short animation with a days-long delay and backwards fill holding a scale on both tags. A paused scale animation on the checklist also passed task 11, failing only tasks 5 and 6. To confirm the drawn size, I loaded each of the five variant pages in the pinned Chromium with no test handling and waited under a second. In every one, the tags' drawn width was not 200px, and the held scale or zoom was still in the computed style. For these pages the task 11 Outcome ('exactly 200px wide on screen') and README line 17 ('It rejects scaling, rotating, translating or zooming a tag or the checklist itself') are false. The lab.json notes have the same problem: they say finite animations are finished first and endless ones are measured as drawn. This is the same class of defect as the accepted cl4-sme-001, and loop 5 narrowed it but did not close it. Graded medium on the same basis as that decision. It needs a deliberate, implausible keyframes rule. The calculated width is still required, because finish() leaves the tag's own base style to be measured, so the box-model calculation is not skipped. The solved-run matrix has no paused or long-running animation variant.
findings.recommendation: Finish only animations that will actually end soon on screen: those that are running (not paused) and whose remaining active time plus delay is short. Measure every other animation as drawn, as the endless ones already are, so that a paused or effectively endless held keyframe fails the existing scale, zoom, width or padding checks. Add a paused variant and a long-duration (or long-delay, backwards-fill) variant to the solved-run matrix, and keep the lab.json notes sentence in line with the rule that ships.

findings.claim: Animations are finished only on the checklist and the two tags, not on their ancestors. A finite scale entrance animation on .page fails task 11 on a private copy of the completed work. The failure is deterministic: it happened on every run, with durations from tens of milliseconds up to seconds, because the headless page is measured before its timeline advances. The message says the tag 'lays out 200px wide but is drawn' at a smaller size and that 'something around it is scaling it'. That is true at the instant measured, but the learner who opens the page sees correct 200px tags once the entrance ends; loading the same page in the pinned Chromium with no test handling and waiting under a second drew both tags at 200px. The same entrance animation on the tags themselves passes, so the behaviour is inconsistent. The lab.json notes sentence 'finite animations finished first' does not say it covers only the checklist and tags. Graded low. A whole-page scale entrance is an unlikely edit in this lab, the error is fail-safe (a correct page fails, no wrong page passes), and the message points at the right region.
findings.recommendation: Settle finite animations on the checklist's ancestors too, using the same rule as cl5-edu-001 (running and ending soon). Or scope the lab.json notes sentence to the checklist and tags, and add a Troubleshooting clause: an animation that scales the page around the checklist must be removed or must have ended.

findings.claim: The tag-side cause list now covers contents, inline*, table*, float and absolute or fixed position. A tag given display: none is not covered. On a private copy of the completed work it fails task 11 on the fill control with no box, and the message blames 'something around the tag (a wrapper, a float beside it, columns or positioning on the checklist)'. README Troubleshooting line 208 says 'the message names the cause', which is not true for this case. The edit is implausible, because the tag vanishes from the page and the learner would notice at once, so this is low polish. One more small wording point: the absolute case prints 'it is positioned absolute', while README line 208 says 'positioned it absolutely'.
findings.recommendation: Treat display: none like display: contents, as a tag-side cause with no box (for example 'its display is none, so it is not drawn'). Optionally print 'it is absolutely positioned' and 'it has fixed position' to match README wording.
